# Hunch CLI reference

Every command, argument and flag, with its default. Run any of them as `npx @kelbie/hunch <command>`.
Unknown flags are refused, and each command lists its own with `--help`.

| Global flag | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `-v, --version` | print the version |
| `--cwd <dir>` | run as if started in this directory |

## `hunch check`

review the lines this branch changed, against your rules

| Argument | Required | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `paths...` | no | only review changes under these paths |

| Flag | Default | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--base <ref>` | `origin/main` | branch to compare against |
| `--head <ref>` |  | compare against this ref instead of the working tree |
| `--staged` |  | review staged changes only |
| `--diff <file>` |  | review a saved unified diff instead of git |
| `--all` |  | review whole files, not just what changed |
| `--task <text>` |  | what the change is meant to do; sent with every hunk |
| `--reporter <format>` | `text` | text, markdown, json, sarif or github |
| `--code` |  | print the changed lines under each finding |
| `--dry-run` |  | count files, hunks and questions without calling Jev |
| `--config <json\|file\|->` |  | rules as JSON instead of a config file; repeatable |
| `--rule <id=text>` |  | add one plain-English rule for this run; repeatable |
| `--only <ids>` |  | ask only these rules, comma-separated; to try a rule you just wrote |
| `--policy-ref <ref>` |  | read config and lock from this ref (the App uses the base commit) |

```text
Exits 0 when the review is complete, 1 when failOnError is set and an error-level concern was
found, and 2 when the review is incomplete or could not run.

Examples:
  hunch check                                 review this branch against origin/main
  hunch check --staged                        review what you are about to commit
  hunch check --base main --head feature/x    review one branch against another
  hunch check --all app/features              review whole files under a path
  hunch check --rule api/errors="Keep the code field on error responses."
  hunch check --config rules.json --reporter json
  hunch check --only api/errors --dry-run     what one rule would cost on this branch
```

## `hunch find`

search existing behavior or find context for a change across the repository

| Argument | Required | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `task` | yes | an intended change, or a yes/no question with --mode condition |
| `paths...` | no | only search under these paths |

| Flag | Default | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--mode <mode>` | `task` | task (change context) or condition (existing behavior) |
| `--chunk-lines <n>` | `150` | maximum lines per source window, 1 to 2000 |
| `--overlap-lines <n>` | `0` | repeat this many lines across source windows |
| `--head <ref>` |  | search a branch or tag instead of the working tree |
| `--facet <list>` |  | only ask these: edit, contract, caller, test, precedent |
| `--min <score>` | `0.5` | drop matches below this score |
| `--top <n>` | `12` | keep at most this many matches per facet; 0 returns all |
| `--lines <n>` | `40` | lines of each passage to print in the terminal |
| `--no-code` | `code` on | print locations only |
| `--concurrency <n>` | `8` | requests in flight, 1 to 32 |
| `--reporter <format>` |  | markdown, text or json (default: text at a terminal, markdown when redirected) |
| `--prs` |  | also ask whether an open pull request already does this |
| `--pr-max <n>` | `10` | pull request diffs to read |
| `--drafts` |  | include draft pull requests |
| `--dry-run` |  | count chunks and requests without calling Jev |
| `--config <json\|file\|->` |  | settings as JSON instead of a config file (include, ignore, provider); repeatable |

```text
Works without a config: it then searches every file, minus lockfiles, minified files and node_modules.
Exits 2 when any chunk or the pull request list could not be searched.

Examples:
  hunch find "add a rate limit to the upload endpoint"
  hunch find "Does this code discard a failed write?" --mode condition --top 0
  hunch find "warn on the onchain receive QR" --prs
  hunch find "rework the feed cache" src/feed --facet test,precedent
  hunch find "add a rate limit" > /tmp/hunch-context.md      Markdown, to hand to a coding agent
```

## `hunch compile`

turn skills and AGENTS.md into review questions, saved in hunch.lock

| Flag | Default | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--with <agent>` |  | claude, codex or gateway; skips the question |
| `--effort <level>` |  | how hard the agent should think |
| `--model <name>` |  | model for the compiling agent |
| `--force` |  | recompile sources that have not changed |
| `--dry-run` |  | list the sources and whether each changed since hunch.lock, without compiling |
| `--reporter <format>` | `text` | text or json |

```text
Examples:
  hunch compile                  asks which installed agent to use
  hunch compile --dry-run        what would be compiled, and what is unchanged
  hunch compile --with claude
  hunch compile --force          rebuild every source
```

## `hunch config`

check the config is valid and show the rules it applies; never edits it

| Flag | Default | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--file <path>` |  | show only the rules asked about this file, overrides applied |
| `--explain <rule>` |  | print exactly what one rule asks Jev, and when it reports |
| `--reporter <format>` | `text` | text or json |
| `--config <json\|file\|->` |  | rules as JSON instead of a config file; repeatable |
| `--rule <id=text>` |  | add one plain-English rule for this run; repeatable |

```text
Exits 2 when the config is invalid, a rule id or reference is missing, or hunch.lock is stale.

Examples:
  hunch config                             is it valid, and which rules are on?
  hunch config --file src/api/upload.ts    which rules are asked about this file?
  hunch config --explain tests/weakened    the question, criteria and state Jev receives
  hunch config --reporter json
```

## `hunch init`

write a config, and optionally a pull request workflow; asks at a terminal, or takes flags

| Flag | Default | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--preset <list>` |  | ts, rust or general, comma-separated (ts,rust for both) |
| `--target <where>` |  | where reviews run: app, actions or local |
| `--github` |  | shorthand for --target actions |
| `--include <glob>` |  | only review files matching this glob; repeatable |
| `--ignore <glob>` |  | skip files matching this glob; repeatable |
| `--fail-on-error` |  | fail the check when an error-level concern is found |
| `--no-zero-data-retention` | `zeroDataRetention` on | don't enforce zero data retention (needed on Vercel Hobby) |
| `--task <pr\|none>` | `pr` | send the PR title and description with each question |
| `--rule <id=text>` |  | add a plain-English rule at warn; repeatable |
| `--install-skill` |  | also install the Hunch agent skill (npx skills add Kelbie/hunch) |
| `-y, --yes` |  | take the detected defaults and ask nothing |

```text
Any flag skips the questions, so agents and CI get the same result every time.

Examples:
  hunch init                                   asks, with arrow keys, and writes the answers
  hunch init --yes                             detected preset, every default, no questions
  hunch init --preset ts,rust --target app     a mixed repository, reviewed by the GitHub App
  hunch init --target actions                  add .github/workflows/hunch.yml too
  hunch init --preset general --no-zero-data-retention --rule api/errors="Error responses keep their code field."
```

## `hunch doctor`

say why this repository is not being reviewed

| Flag | Default | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--app <slug>` | `hunch-review` | the App to look for |
| `--reporter <format>` | `text` | text or json |

```text
Checks the config on the default branch, the App installation, and the Actions workflow and secret,
using your gh login. Exits 1 when a check fails; a fact it cannot establish is "unknown", never "ok".

Examples:
  hunch doctor
  hunch doctor --app my-hunch-app --reporter json
```

## `hunch eval`

measure each rule's precision and recall on labelled .diff examples

| Argument | Required | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dir` | yes | directory of .diff fixtures |

| Flag | Default | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--config <json\|file\|->` |  | rules as JSON instead of a config file; repeatable |
| `--rule <id=text>` |  | add one plain-English rule for this run; repeatable |
| `--reporter <format>` | `text` | text or json |

```text
Each fixture is a .diff whose first line is "# expect: rule-a, rule-b" (the rules that should fire).

Examples:
  hunch eval examples/presets
  hunch eval fixtures --rule api/errors="Error responses keep their code field." --reporter json
```

## `hunch app register`

register a GitHub App from a manifest, in your browser

| Flag | Default | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--name <name>` |  | the App's name (required) |
| `--webhook-url <url>` |  | https://HOST/api/webhook (required) |
| `--organization <org>` |  | register it to an organisation instead of your account |
| `--public` |  | let any account install it |

## `hunch app connect`

upload production credentials and set the webhook

| Flag | Default | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--app-id <id>` |  | the App ID from register (required) |
| `--webhook-url <url>` |  | https://HOST/api/webhook (required) |
| `--vercel-project <name>` |  | Vercel project to upload secrets to (required) |
| `--scope <team>` |  | Vercel team scope (required) |
| `--private-key <path>` |  | PEM file, for an App connecting for the first time |
